question: Secondary post-tonsillectomy haemorrhage most commonly occurs on days 5 to 10 after surgery due to sloughing of the tonsillar bed eschar, and should be treated as a surgical emergency regardless of the apparent severity of bleeding.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Secondary haemorrhage peaks at days 5-10 due to eschar sloughing. The danger is the 'sentinel bleed' — a small bleed that precedes a massive haemorrhage. All cases must be admitted and treated as surgical emergencies, not managed expectantly at home.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Secondary haemorrhage (days 5-10, peak around day 7-8) results from eschar separation. Even apparently minor bleeding can herald a catastrophic sentinel bleed — all cases require hospital admission, IV access, group and crossmatch, and ENT review. 'Wait and watch' at home is never appropriate.
